items.followUp: Write two characteristics of a good algorithm.

rubric.why: Identifies that an algorithm consists of a limited sequence or set of instructions.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm is a finite sequence or set of instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the instructions as a finite sequence or set.

rubric.why: States the purpose of the algorithm.
rubric.description: Says the instructions are for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the algorithm solves a problem.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions.
These instructions are followed to solve a particular problem.

items.followUp: What is meant by an unambiguous solution?

rubric.why: Captures the clear nature of a candid solution.
rubric.description: States that a candid solution is clear and straightforward.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the solution as clear or straightforward.

rubric.why: Shows that the solution should not be open to different interpretations.
rubric.description: States that each step has a definite meaning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the solution is unambiguous or definite.

modelAnswer: A candid solution is a clear and straightforward solution to a problem.
Its steps have definite meanings and are not open to confusion.

items.followUp: What is the use of a decision symbol in an algorithm?

rubric.why: Identifies the control-transfer function of GOTO notation.
rubric.description: States that GOTO transfers control to another step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it transfers control or jumps to a specified step.

rubric.description: Mentions a specified step, step number, or label as the destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the destination of the transfer.

modelAnswer: GOTO notation transfers control from the current step to another specified step in an algorithm.
The destination is usually identified by a step number or label.

items.followUp: How can an algorithm help before writing a computer program?

rubric.why: Explains that an algorithm gives an ordered plan for solving a problem.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm lays out the solution step by step.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its step-by-step plan.

rubric.why: Connects the algorithm to understanding or solving the problem, or preparing a program.
rubric.description: Explains that the plan helps solve the problem or can guide program development.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating a relevant problem-solving or program-development benefit.

modelAnswer: An algorithm provides an ordered, step-by-step plan for solving a problem.
It helps us understand the solution and use it to develop a program.

items.followUp: Write HTML code that displays an image as a hyperlink to another web page.

rubric.why: Checks that the image is placed inside a hyperlink anchor.
rubric.description: Uses an anchor tag with an href attribute for the link destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing the anchor/href part of the method.

rubric.why: Checks that the image is inserted and nested inside the anchor.
rubric.description: Includes an image tag with its source inside the anchor tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the image tag/source as the clickable content.

modelAnswer: Write an anchor tag and set its href attribute to the page or address to open.
Place the image tag inside the anchor tag, for example: .

items.followUp: What is the full form of HTML, and what is it used to create?

rubric.why: Checks the correct expansion of the abbreviation HTML.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of HTML.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: Checks the basic purpose of HTML.
rubric.description: States that HTML is used to create or structure web pages.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming web pages or websites as its purpose.

modelAnswer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.
It is used to create and structure web pages.

items.followUp: Which digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: Checks the base of the binary number system.
rubric.description: Identifies binary as a base-2 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its base is 2.

rubric.why: Checks the digits used in binary representation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both 0 and 1.

modelAnswer: The binary number system is a positional number system with base 2.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: What kinds of information can be stored in computer memory?

rubric.why: Defines memory as a storage component or area.
rubric.description: States that computer memory is used for storage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying memory as a place or area for storing information.

rubric.why: Names information stored in computer memory.
rubric.description: Mentions data and/or instructions stored in memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming data or instructions as stored information.

modelAnswer: Computer memory is the storage area of a computer.
It stores data and instructions needed for processing.
